en: So, where do we start?
We'll start with a life hack.
Someone asked us for more life hacks.
So, it's really important at the start of training that the surface
here doesn't match the surface here.
For example, a bare knee and some fabric on the elbow.
Or the other way round: fabric — say, pants on the knees — and a bare
elbow. Why? So it doesn't slip. If your knee keeps sliding
off the elbow — man, it'll be really hard to train. Or you can
do one thing: put on an elbow pad —
or roll it up like I've done now, so there's a ridge here.
On that ridge it's much easier to train this freeze. You'll
go up and really feel stable — it'll be great. That's
important. Or you can wear a knee pad and nothing on the elbow —
that's stable too. Start with these things first. So how
do people start? Everyone starts out wrong: they put this hand
here, this one here, and get into a position like this. But the other
hand — I'm on my left — the other hand has to be in line with the left one.
Let me face you head-on.
So if I do it here, my body lines up, and I
have to put my hand right here.
It shouldn't be over here.
Because if you train it wrong, you'll learn to shift
your body weight wrong.
Actually, you won't learn to shift your weight at all.
In this freeze it's key to learn to shift your weight along one line.
Notice that I'm in one line,

balance. That's important.
Let me show it like this too.

making one line.
So you have to shift from this position into this one.
Bending the body a little into this position.
